title: Fix PBKDF2 iterations: 210k exceeds Cloudflare's platform cap
description:
BLOCKER found by the first live deploy (https://ticks-factory.pe-1a0.workers.dev). cloud/factory/src/auth.ts ships DEFAULT_ITERATIONS = 210_000 and MAX_ITERATIONS = 1_000_000. Cloudflare Workers caps PBKDF2 at 100_000 iterations: crypto.subtle.deriveBits THROWS on the edge above that, so every authenticated request returns 503 auth_not_configured on a correctly deployed factory.

Measured live, same token, same code, only the iteration count changed:
- 210_000 -> 503 (deriveBits throws)
- 100_000 -> 404 on /api/runs (authenticated; route simply does not exist yet). Also verified: no token -> 401, wrong token -> 401.

Three fixes, all needed:
1. DEFAULT_ITERATIONS and MAX_ITERATIONS must both be <= 100_000. Note aro's own concern #2: the token is 256 bits of CSPRNG output, so stretching buys nothing against brute force the way it does for a password — going lower is defensible on the merits, not just the cap.
2. authenticateFactoryRequest's catch reports EVERY throw as 'not a valid <scheme> record'. That is wrong and it actively misdirected diagnosis: /health said configured:true (parse succeeded) while the request path said the record was invalid (crypto threw). Distinguish a parse failure from a crypto/runtime failure and say which.
3. Local workerd does NOT enforce the cap — 60/60 tests passed on a value that cannot work in production. Add a guard test asserting DEFAULT_ITERATIONS <= 100_000 and MAX_ITERATIONS <= 100_000, with a comment citing the platform limit, so no future change can reintroduce this without a red test.

The live deployment currently runs a hand-pushed 100k record so it works; the code does not.
acceptance_criteria: DEFAULT_ITERATIONS and MAX_ITERATIONS are both <= 100_000; a test fails if either is raised above the cap; the auth middleware distinguishes parse failure from crypto failure in its 503 detail and logs; existing auth tests still pass.
